provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the Tours Mame 1922 (editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam) layer reads 'tux' where the 1962 prints 'tuae'; recogniser damage, letterforms inferred not read; conclusion length only: the 1962 continues 'nostrum Iesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit' where the Tours Mame 1922 (editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam) stops at the short cue; conclusion length only: the Tours Mame 1922 (editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam) stops at the short cue; the words that follow it in the witness ('Missis non conyentualibus, Vigilie Ss. Petri') are the book's own rubric, not part of the prayer, and the 1962 continues 'unitate.'; pointing was NOT collated: this comparison is word-level, because the witness reaches me as an optical text layer whose commas, colons and full stops are unreliable. Corroboration: Pustet Ratisbon 1862: Pustet Ratisbon 1862, printed p. 2 (nearest preceding printed-folio marker at text-layer line 93507); text-layer lines 97382-97390 (word-coverage of the 1962 body 0.882). Recorded limitation: Antecedent taken from the Tours Mame 1922 (editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam). Word-coverage of the 1962 body at this locus 0.941, of the whole oration 0.75. Every 1862 and Mame reading in this lane rests on an optical text layer, not on a page image; 2 word(s) in this passage were damaged by the recogniser and were read against the 1962 wording rather than off the page - L56861 'Irenzo' read as 'ireneo'; L56865 'Ecclesiz' read as 'ecclesie'. What was NOT checked: the pointing, the ornamental initials, and the printed page of the 1862 beyond the nearest folio marker.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui beato Irenaeo Martyri tuo atque Pontifici tribuisti, ut et
veritate doctrinae expugnaret haereses, et pacem Ecclesiae feliciter
confirmaret: da, quaesumus, plebi tuae in sancta religione constantiam; et
pacem tuam nostris concede temporibus. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum,
Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Historical source s-irenaei-episcopi-martyris/main/Collect/all/1; same-witness-conclusion-table. Complete petitions equal and actual Latin conclusion prefixes match the same printed family through-our-lord at passage.francis-xavier-lasance.the-new-roman-missal.benziger-revised-1945.resume-orations-conclusion-table-2026-10-23-verify; tracked rule/formula passage.francis-xavier-lasance.the-new-roman-missal.benziger-revised-1945.resume-orations-conclusion-table-2026-10-23-transcription. translations.text: O God, Who didst vouchsafe unto blessed Irenaeus, Thy martyr and bishop; by his strenuous teaching of the truth, utterly to confute heresies, and happily to establish peace in Thy Church: unto us Thy people, grant, we beseech Thee, to be steadfast in the practice of our holy religion, and in all our days to enjoy that peace which is from Thee. Through our Lord.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Deus, qui credentes in te populos nullis sinis concuti terroribus: dignare
preces et hostias dicatae tibi plebis suscipere; ut pax, a tua pietate
concessa, christianorum fines ab omni hoste faciat esse securos. Per
Dominum.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Deus, auctor pacis et amator, quem nosse vivere, cui servire regnare est:
protege ab omnibus impugnationibus supplices tuos; ut, qui in defensione tua
confidimus, beati Irenaei Martyris tui atque Pontificis intercessione,
nullius hostilitatis arma timeamus. Per Dominum.

translations.text: O God, the author and lover of peace, to know Whom is to live, and to serve Whom is to reign, protect us Thy suppliants from all assaults, that we, who trust in Thy defense, by the intercession of blessed Irenaeus, Thy martyr and bishop, may not fear the arms of any of our foes. Through our Lord.
